summary: Add soft mission targetAt and ordered milestones with rich Effect instant authoring

replay.detail: No event or projection rule change. Absent fields preserve existing serialized mission bytes and revision hashes.

schema.detail: Mission declarations accept optional target-at and milestone ID at fields. Instants use an explicit-known-offset RFC3339 profile with millisecond precision and normalize to UTC. Milestone IDs are unique and instants strictly increasing. TypeScript decodes authoring values to Effect DateTime.Utc; native metadata is only targetAt plus milestones with id and at. Graph-to-program lowering refuses date metadata instead of silently discarding it.

rules.detail: Dates and milestones have no runtime effect until a delivery slice exists. They do not authorize, schedule, cancel, notify, mark completion or change execution timeouts.

compatibility.detail: No client-v0 schema or codegen changes. Follow-up #6887: a reader capability check enforced at publish, in the same proposed capability mechanism as mission-escalation-v1, requiring mission-dates-v1 before publishing target or milestone metadata. That gate is not implemented by this schema-only slice; old readers must never silently drop milestones.

downtime.detail: No startup or daemon lifecycle changes.

manual.detail: Do not publish or use mission date metadata until the follow-up publish-time mission-dates-v1 reader capability gate is implemented and all supported readers advertise support. Milestones have no effect until delivery exists.

recovery.detail: Remove target and milestone metadata and republish before rolling back to readers without date support.
